The brief facts of the case as per claim petition are that on 18.10.2014 at about 07:30 p.m., Duli Chand (since deceased) along with his son Bhupender (petitioner no.3 herein) was going from village Chaprola to Ghaziabad by motorcycle bearing registration no. UP16-AC-7532, being driven by Bhupender and when they reached opposite Samtal Factory, G.T. Road, District G.B. Nagar, U.P.,
all of a sudden, a truck bearing registration no. HR64C-1671 (in short "offending vehicle"), being driven by respondent no.1 rashly and negligently, hit the motorcycle with a great force.

As a result,

Duli Chand, who was pillion rider of the said motorcycle, sustained serious injuries and was taken to Sudarshan Hospital, where he was declared dead.

His postmortem was conduced at Mortuary, G.B.
Nagar, U.P.
In connection with the accident, FIR no.360/2014, under sections 279/338/304-A IPC was registered at PS Badalpur, District G.B. Nagar, U.P.

By way of present claim petition, claimants alleged that the accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle which was being driven by respondent no.1, owned by respondent no.2 and insured with respondent no.3 at the time of accident and thus, claimed a compensation of Rs.20 lakhs along with interest @
12% per annum from the respondents.
3. In response to the notice of claim petition, all the respondents put their appearance and filed replies/ written-statements.
In the joint written-statement filed on behalf of respondent no.1 and 2, it is stated that the alleged offending vehicle has been falsely implicated in the accident.

Further, it is stated that the vehicle was duly insured with respondent no.3/ insurance company and therefore, liability, if any, to pay the compensation can be fastened upon the insurance company only.
3.2

In the written-statement filed on behalf of respondent no.3/ insurance company, it has been fairly admitted that the offending vehicle was insured with them at the relevant time, however, they contended that their liability is subject to compliance of terms and conditions of the insurance policy.

4. Upon completion of pleadings, my learned predecessor framed the issues on 16.03.2016, as under:
i).

Whether respondent no.1 was driving vehicle bearing no.
HR64C-1671 on 18.10.2014 at 07:30 p.m., opposite Samtal Factory, G.B. Nagar, U.P. at a high speed and in rash and negligent manner and hit against motorcycle bearing no. UP16AC-7532, being driven by Bhupender with deceased Duli Chand as pillion rider, as a result, its occupant namely Duli Chand fell down and sustained fatal injuries?
OPP ii).
Whether the petitioners are entitled for any compensation, if so, for what amount?
OPP (iii). Relief.

Komal and two sons Naitik Kumar and Lovish Kumar as his legal heirs.
Death certificate of petitioner no.4 was placed on record.
Accordingly, application was allowed and amended memo of parties showing legal heirs of deceased petitioner no.4 Mahesh Kumar, was taken on record.

9. My findings on the issues are as under:
Whether respondent no.1 was driving vehicle bearing no. HR64C-1671 on 18.10.2014 at 07:30 p.m., opposite Samtal Factory, G.B. Nagar, U.P. at a high speed and in rash and negligent manner and hit against motorcycle bearing no. UP16AC-7532, being driven by Bhupender with deceased Duli Chand as pillion rider
, as a result, its occupant namely Duli Chand fell down and sustained fatal injuries?
OPP 10.
On this issue, the testimony of eye-witness PW2 Bhupender is relevant to be discussed here.

PW2 testified that on 18.10.2014, he along with his father Sh. Duli Chand (deceased) and his daughter Shristi was going from village Chaprola to District Ghaziabad on motorcycle bearing no.
UP16AC-7532, which was being driven by him (PW2) at slow speed and carefully and when they reached opposite Samtal Factory, G.T. Road, District G.B. Nagar, U.P. , all of a sudden, the offending truck bearing no. HR64C-1671, being driven by its driver rashly and negligently, came and hit their motorcycle.

As a result, their motorcycle fell down and his father Duli Chand sustained grievous injuries and he was taken to Sudershan Hospital, where doctors declared him dead and postmortem of dead body was conducted at Mortuary, G.B. Nagar, U.P. PW2 further deposed that he ______________________________________________________________________

U.P. He categorically deposed that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by respondent no.1.
During cross- examination also, this witness clarified that the offending vehicle was a truck bearing no. HR64-C-1671 which was driven rashly and they got hit by the said truck from back side.
I may note that the only suggestion given to this witness by learned counsel for the respondents to the effect that he was not the eye-witness of the accident, has been promptly denied by him.
11. Having gone through the entire deposition of the eye-witness, I find that his testimony has remained consistent and unshaken during the cross-examination.

Further, respondents did not lead any evidence to prove the defence taken in their written-statements that driver/ respondent no.1 did not cause the accident and he has been falsely implicated in this case.

The evidence of eye-witness (PW2) on the aspect of rash and negligent act of respondent no.1 while driving the offending vehicle has remained unimpeached and hence, the same is to be accepted on its face value itself.
12.

Further, the respondent no.1, driver of the offending vehicle was the best witness, who could have stepped into the witness box to challenge the testimony of eye-witness (PW2) regarding the above accident and its manner but he preferred not to enter into the witness box during the course of inquiry.

Thus, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against him to the effect that the accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by him in view of the law laid down in case of Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Kamlesh, 2009 (3) AD (Delhi) 310.

The FIR was registered in the matter without delay and after detailed investigation, respondent no.1 was charge-sheeted in the criminal case and in cases of motor vehicle accident claims, contents of charge-sheet are admissible in evidence and deemed to be correct under Rule 7 of Delhi Motor Accident Tribunal Rules, 2008, which support the testimony of eye- witnesses regarding rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by respondent no.1.

14. The Site Plan which is part of the criminal case record Ex.PW1/1 (colly) also supports the manner of accident as per version of the eye- witness (PW2).
15.
Thus, the facts that FIR has been registered and charge sheet has also been filed against the respondent no.1 by the police, are sufficient proof to conclude that respondent no.1 was negligent.

Reliance is placed upon the judgment of Hon'ble Delhi High Court in the case titled as Shabina v.
Satvir & Ors. MAC. APP. 980/17 dated 24.01.2020, wherein Hon'ble Delhi High Court observed that in so far as FIR has been registered, criminal case has been initiated against driver of offending vehicle and vehicle was seized, the requirement of proving the preponderance of probability of accident having been caused by rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle has been established.

sentences.text: ON perusal of the award of the Tribunal, it becomes clear that the wife of the deceased had produced (I) certified copy of the criminal record of criminal case in FIR No. 955/2004, pertaining to involvement of the offending vehicle, (ii) Criminal record showing completion of investigation of police and issue of charge sheet under Section 279/304-A IPC against the driver, (iii) certified copy of FIR, wherein criminal case against the driver was lodged; and (iv) recovery memo and mechanical inspection report of offending vehicle and vehicle of the deceased.
These documents are sufficient proofs to reach the conclusion that the driver was negligent.
Proceedings under Motor Vehicles Act are not akin to proceedings in a civil suit and hence strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard.
Hence, this contention of the counsel of the appellant also falls face down.
There is ample evidence on record to prove negligence on the part of driver."
16. Moreover, it is settled law that in an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.

Reference may be made to the judgments titled as 'New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v.
Sakshi Bhutani & Others', MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012, 'Bimla Devi & Others v.
Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others' (2009) 13 SC 530, 'Parmeshwari v. Amirchand ______________________________________________________________________ & Others' 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & 'Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others', 2018,
Law Suit (SC) 303.

To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
Step-1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balance which is considered to be the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Step-2 (Ascertaining the multiplier)
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
The multiplier should be chosen from the said table with reference to the age of the deceased.
Step-3 (Actual Calculation)

The annual contribution to the family (multiplicand)
when multiplied by such multiplier gives the 'loss of dependency' to the family.
Thereafter, a conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000/- to Rs.10,000/- may be added as loss of estates.
Where the deceased is survived by his widow, another conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000 to Rs.10,000 should be added under the head of loss of consortium.
But no amount is to be awarded under the head of pain, suffering or hardship caused to the legal heirs of the deceased.
__ __ __ The funeral expenses, cost of transportation of the body (if incurred) and the cost of any medical treatment of the deceased before death (if incurred) should also be added."

In view of the aforesaid judgment, it is essential to take into consideration the following parameters:-
PECUNIARY DAMAGES:
Age of deceased :
22.
The age of deceased Dulichand has been mentioned as 54 years in the claim petition.
Further, I may find that in the Panchnama prepared by police and in the postmortem report prepared at District Mortuary, G. B. Nagar, U.P, the age of deceased is mentioned as 54 years.
Thus, age of deceased on the date of accident is to be taken as 54 years.

Assessment of Income of deceased :
23.

PW3 Phoolwati deposed that her husband Duli Chand (deceased) was working as driver in Sanskar Public School, Roja Jalalpur, District G.B. Nagar, U.P and was earning Rs.15,000/- per month but she did not produce any documentary evidence in support of her claim.
The claim petition reflects the address of all the petitioners as that of U.P.
The accident of deceased also occurred in U.P.

In the circumstances, in the absence of any documentary evidence in respect of education and income of deceased, his income may be considered at par with minimum wages of unskilled worker prevalent in the State of U.P on the date of accident (18.10.2014), which were Rs.6,416/- per month.
Thus, the income of the deceased for computing the loss of income would be considered to be Rs.6,416/- per month.
The age of deceased was 54 years at the time of accident.
An appropriate multiplier has to be determined for computation of compensation.
The judgment titled as Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121 is relevant to consider the multiplier.

In Para 21 of the judgment, the guidelines for the multiplier were laid down in accordance with age are as under:-
 MULTIPLIER AGE GROUP OF DECEASED  M-18 Age groups between 15 to 20 &

In view of the above said judgment, a multiplier of 11 has to be applied against 54 years of age of the deceased to determine the compensation.

"(iii) While determining the income, an addition of 50% of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a ______________________________________________________________________ permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.
The addition should be 30%, if the age of the deceased was between 40 to 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years, the addition should be 15%.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.
(iv) In case the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40% of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.
An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component.
(viii) Reasonable figures on conventional heads, namely, loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be Rs. 15,000/-, Rs. 40,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively.
The aforesaid amounts should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years."
26. The deceased can be considered a self-employed.
In view of the above said judgment, an addition of 10% of the income of deceased who belonged to age group 50 to 60 years, has to be considered towards future prospects.

Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.
